title: Spotting the endings ing and ed
examples: Why does ed sound like t?

figure.name: x-word
figure.note: Find the word you know first.

explain.say: Long words often have a little tail on the end. Look at jumping on the board. Here is a trick: find the word you know first, then read the tail.

draw.text: Spotting the endings ing and ed

draw.name: x-word
draw.note: Find the word you know first.

explain.say: Look at the first part glowing: jump. You already know that word! Jump on the spot and say it.

draw.name: x-word
draw.note: Find the word you know first.

explain.say: Now the tail: ing. It sounds like the end of sing. It tells you something is happening. Jump plus ing: jumping! Can you say, I am jumping?

draw.name: x-word
draw.note: Find the word you know first.

explain.say: Here is another tail: ed. It tells you something already happened. Play plus ed: played. In played, the ed sounds like d. What did you play yesterday?
Here is a funny thing: ed can make three different sounds! Look at the three groups on the board. Brilliant work! Challenge: which group does the word skated go in?

faq.q: What does ing mean on the end of a word?
faq.a: ing tells you something is happening, like jumping, playing or reading. It sounds like the end of sing.

faq.q: What does ed mean on the end of a word?
faq.a: ed usually tells you something already happened, like jumped, played or painted.

faq.q: Why does ed sound different in different words?
faq.a: ed can sound like t, as in jumped, like d, as in played, or like id, as in painted. Your mouth picks the easiest one to say.
asks: Why does jumped sound like jumpt?

faq.q: How do I read a word with an ending?
faq.a: Cover the ending with your finger and read the base word. Then uncover the ending and add it on. An ending like ing or ed is called a suffix.

faq.q: Why does hopping have two p letters?
faq.a: When a short word like hop gets ing, we often double the last letter. Hop becomes hopping. That keeps the o short, so it does not turn into hoping.

facts: The ending ed can sound like t in jumped, d in played, or id in painted.
Endings like ing and ed are called suffixes.
